questions.question: Where can I study on Busch campus late at night?

runs.question: Where can I study on Busch campus late at night?
runs.answer: According to a student post in `campus_why_no_24_hour_library.txt`, ARC and SERC on Busch are both open 24 hours, so you can find an open classroom there. The same student suggested going to the second floor of SERC for more privacy, specifically near the stairwell at the end of the TA office hallway.

retrieved.label: campus_why_no_24_hour_library.txt#2
retrieved.text:
THREAD: why no 24 hour library

--- reply 3 (29 votes) ---
If you’re on Busch, ARC and SERC are both open 24 hours, so you should be able to find an open classroom. If you want more privacy, go to the second floor of SERC. Go through the door leading to the TA office hallway. Back in the day, I moved a table to the end of that hallway near the stairwell. That was my secret spot and nobody goes there..

retrieved.label: campus_why_no_24_hour_library.txt#0
retrieved.text:
THREAD: why no 24 hour library

i wish there was a 24 hour library somewhere on campus. yes i can study all i want in the residence lounges but its not as motivating cause id rather just be in my room. technically you can go in the buildings after hours but then id be on edge of someone coming and asking why i was there.

idk man im a night owl so by the time i get into a good flow i have to leave the library which sucks

retrieved.label: housing_ultimate_guide_to_on_campus_housing_for_continuing_student.txt#21
retrieved.text:
THREAD: Ultimate Guide to On-Campus Housing for Continuing Students
TOPIC: Housing

--- reply 5 (4 votes) ---
It depends on what you apply for.

For Busch Suites it’s nearly impossible to get in unless you have 6 sophomores (no juniors, freshmen or seniors) since reverse seniority points are required for suites (and freshmen can’t get suites.)

Other dorms such as the BAMM complex are reserved solely for freshmen and their upperclassmen RAs

For BEST you need to apply separately

Idk about other things but it really depends on the type of dorm you want more than the campus (though some campuses, like CA, are more popular than Douglass, for example.)

I don’t know how easy it is to get into generic dorms on busch outside of BAMM but if you have a decent housing number you’ll be fine.

questions.question: What should I think about before converting a class to Pass/No Credit?

runs.question: What should I think about before converting a class to Pass/No Credit?
runs.answer: According to a student post in academics_pass_no_credit_faq_as_it_stands_right_now_way_before_the_p.txt, you should consider that P/NC classes will count toward majors and prerequisites that only need a C, but you should contact an advisor if a class requires a B (such as Math300 CS or financial accounting), as the rules get murky. The author also recommends consulting an advisor prior to making your decision.

retrieved.label: academics_pass_no_credit_faq_as_it_stands_right_now_way_before_the_p.txt#0
retrieved.text:
THREAD: Pass/No Credit FAQ as it stands right now way before the Provost puts it up

Disclaimer: Everything said here can change, however at the moment this is how things be rolling

First and foremost: you can choose which classes to convert your grade to pass/no credit. You can do all. You can do some. You can do none.

Second: you can choose up until May 22nd to convert your letter grade to a P or NC. Yes you can fail shit and then save your GPA after finding out you failed at least as the policy stands right now

Third: a P or NC grade will not change GPA. Hypothetically if you P/NC every single class you’re taking, your gpa will neither increase nor decrease from what it stands at the end of Fall 2019

retrieved.label: academics_pass_no_credit_faq_as_it_stands_right_now_way_before_the_p.txt#2
retrieved.text:
THREAD: Pass/No Credit FAQ as it stands right now way before the Provost puts it up

Professors will not know if you aren’t taking a letter grade in their class. The professor is required to submit a letter grade. The registrar will convert the grade if you have requested it. The professor will not know that it got converted

Drop for a W deadline is now 4/10

The form to request P/NC is not out yet. Be patient

retrieved.label: academics_pass_no_credit_faq_as_it_stands_right_now_way_before_the_p.txt#3
retrieved.text:
THREAD: Pass/No Credit FAQ as it stands right now way before the Provost puts it up

That is all. Understand this policy is much much more favorable for us than other schools. Many have set a deadline to chose around early-mid April. So try to be accepting of this rather than pushing for more (like that universal pass everyone gets a pass bullshit).

retrieved.label: academics_pass_no_credit_faq_as_it_stands_right_now_way_before_the_p.txt#1
retrieved.text:
THREAD: Pass/No Credit FAQ as it stands right now way before the Provost puts it up

Here’s the most important one for r/Rutgers: P/NC CLASSES WILL COUNT TOWARD MAJORS, PREREQUISITES, WHATEVER ELSE that only needs a C to happen. If you need a B, (Math300 CS, financial accounting) contact an advisor. The waters get murky with the B required rules. My source on this (the first part) is Dr. G himself. Consulting an advisor prior to making the decision is recommended

Additional notes:

retrieved.label: data_did_i_cook.txt#1
retrieved.text:
THREAD: Did I cook?

--- reply 2 (2 votes) ---
HELL YEA
fellow 18 credit-er here: it’s not AS bad as people say as long as you take good courses! I took 3 4-credit classes and 2 3-credit ones, so still the usual 5. even while working full time, I got 4 A’s and 1 89 (still upset but w/e). so hell yea I applaud you for working hard and getting the results for it!! those weren’t easy classes either, so you definitely deserve the kudos!

THREAD: Professor Needing Student Advice with Online Course (Starts Tomorrow)

--- reply 3 (30 votes) ---
